`first_chunk_at - started_at`. A retry after a failed attempt or a dropped
stream keeps the first try's `started_at`, so after a retry the difference
can also include the failed tries and the wait between them (as

sources.claim: started_at (api_start_time) has one assignment repo-wide, once per API call before the retry loop
the retry loop re-runs build_api_request for every try and leaves api_start_time alone
pre_api_request fires per try with the same started_at; first_chunk_at is reset per try
the error path measures elapsed time across tries from the unchanged api_start_time
api_duration = now - api_start_time, so api_duration/ended_at always span every try
a dropped chat-completions/Anthropic stream reconnects inside one try after a backoff, and each reopened stream gets fresh diagnostics (first_chunk_at comes from the stream that answered)
the Codex Responses runner sets first_chunk_at only while it is None, across its own physical stream retry, so the difference may or may not include a failed Codex stream (hence 'can also include')

restarts (compression, redirect, length continuation, rebuilt-for-fallback) leave the retry loop and start a new outer iteration with a fresh api_start_time, so the text speaks of retries, not restarts
